title: The Teleofunctional Evolutionary Representation Model (TERM): A Formal Continuity of Meaning
content: The ontological transition from biological signaling to the complexities of human natural language has traditionally been conceptualized as a saltational leap—a categorical rupture where mechanical causality terminates and "rational" intentionality emerges. This paper posits the Teleofunctional Evolutionary Representation Model (TERM) as a robust framework to bridge this theoretical lacuna. By synthesizing Ruth Millikan’s biosemantics with a novel structural-functional taxonomic unit termed the "Functure," this study argues for a formal, teleological continuity extending from primordial genetic sequences (R0) to the sophisticated structures of formal logic (R3). The analysis provides a rigorous critique of the rationalist tradition, which erroneously treats representation as an exclusively mental phenomenon. Instead, it is proposed that intentionality constitutes a natural property derived from the evolutionary efficacy of producer-consumer systems. The model culminates in a redefinition of logic: rather than a collection of transcendental Platonic laws, logic is understood as the stabilized regulation of representational transitions, selected to facilitate inter-agent social coordination. This exploration offers a naturalized account of semantics, displacing the "subjective mind" from the locus of meaning and repositioning it as an emergent product of teleofunctional history.
